title: Run a three-library mutation campaign to 85 percent each
goal: This is the band capstone: one shared pytest suite under work/gc-359/tests/ must simultaneously push slugify/slugify.py (105 mutants), inflection/__init__.py (286 mutants), and jmespath/lexer.py (262 mutants) each past an 85 percent kill rate, scored as the minimum of the three. A naive snapshot suite reaches roughly 73 percent on slugify alone, so the last dozen points per library only fall to survivor-by-survivor triage: read each mutant diff, decide killable versus suspected-equivalent, and construct the single input that separates the mutant from the original. The campaign needs an explicit cross-library schedule, per-library survivor ledgers, and recovery when a grading run shows the minimum stuck while total kills rise; the whole suite must stay under 3 seconds or grading disqualifies. Fail-closed grading: red baseline, slow suite, source-introspection tokens, or mutant-total drift in any of the three modules scores min_module_kill_rate -1.
resources: pypi python-slugify==8.0.4 (+ text-unidecode==1.3), inflection==0.5.1, jmespath==1.0.1 (three targets under mutation)
pypi mutmut==2.4.4 + parso==0.8.4 (deterministic mutant generation; all transitive deps pinned in assets/gc-359/config.json)
pypi pytest==8.2.2 (only permitted test framework; plugin autoload disabled at grading time)
files under assets/gc-359/ (sealed grader grade.py + config.json with expected mutant totals)
process_expectations: A behavior-inventory plan exists at work/gc-359/plan.md, written before the first grading run, mapping the target module's behaviors to planned test groups.
At least two full grading runs are logged under work/gc-359/logs/ as raw grader JSON lines, and the survivor count decreases between the first and the last run.
Surviving mutants are tracked by mutant ID (mutmut result-ids / mutmut show) at work/gc-359/survivors.md, each with a verdict of killable-next or suspected-equivalent -- identities, not just counts.
A cross-library schedule exists in work/gc-359/plan.md and per-library survivor ledgers are updated after every grading run, with the binding (minimum) library named each time.
Every RED or disqualified grading run is recorded with its cause and the concrete recovery action taken; no silent retries.
